subject_entity.title_display: De Ecclesiae Catholicae Unitate (On the Unity of the Church)
subject_entity.notes: Cyprian's most influential treatise c. 251; argues that the unity of the Church is grounded in the unity of the episcopate; the see of Peter is the source and origin of episcopal unity; each bishop holds the whole of the one episcopate in solidum; schism and heresy are worse than apostasy because they rend the body of Christ; foundational text for Catholic ecclesiology.

object_entity.notes: Bishop of Carthage c. 248–258; major Latin theologian of ecclesiology and sacramental theology; converted c. 246; deeply influenced by Tertullian; key figure in the Novatian controversy (supported Cornelius against Novatian); martyred under Valerian.

evidence.notes: Cyprian is the author of De Unitate.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: The Lord says to Peter: I say unto thee that thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. And to thee will I give the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Upon him he builds the Church, and to him he gives the command to feed the sheep. And although he assigns an equal power to all the apostles, yet he established one chair, and arranged by his authority the source and reason of unity. The other apostles were also what Peter was, but the primacy is given to Peter to show that there is one Church and one chair.
passage.notes: Petrine primacy as source of episcopal unity; one chair, one Church
